title: Musely vs FutureClinic: the spot cream subscription or a dermatologist's prescription
summary: Musely vs FutureClinic compares Musely's Spot Cream cost per month with a $40 FutureClinic doctor visit, pharmacy choice, and no subscription required.
body_markdown:
[Musely](https://www.musely.com/) and FutureClinic both treat[melasma](https://futureclinic.com/blog/melasma-treatment-online-dermatologist-by-message) , dark spots, and acne by message, and unlike Curology or Agency, where visits may go to a[nurse practitioner](https://futureclinic.com/blog/nurse-practitioner-vs-doctor-who-treats-you-online) , physician assistant, or physician, both services state that doctors treat you. Where they differ is how your care and prescriptions work: Musely pairs a $20 visit fee with its own compounded formulas on a two-month auto-refill plan or one-time purchase, while FutureClinic connects you with a physician for a $40 best-fit visit (or typically $20 to $100 for a chosen doctor) who can prescribe any appropriate brand or generic medicine to the pharmacy you choose with no subscription required.


Every clinician on FutureClinic is a state-licensed, background-checked, verified physician holding an MD, DO or MBBS degree, never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant, as we believe people's health deserves expert-level care. No form is approved in bulk: a specific doctor reads your full case and replies with a Human Signature, a short video or voice note recorded live for you. You can message that same doctor time after time, however long in between. For melasma or acne, staying with the same doctor lets you build trust, try treatments together, swap an irritating cream, step down strength as dark patches fade, and track progress over months. Your doctor can also help with other problems in their specialty, and every FutureClinic doctor you see shares[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) .


Your doctor's only incentive on FutureClinic is to help you. Your physician earns nothing extra when ordering tests or prescribing, and FutureClinic sells no products, removing any reason to upsell a cream or lab panel. Keeping your prescription active never depends on staying subscribed month after month. If your doctor decides a prescription is right for you, they can prescribe whichever brand or generic fits, with no house formulary to steer them, to the pharmacy you choose.


## How do Musely and FutureClinic compare side by side?


Feature Musely FutureClinic


**Who treats you** "Board-Certified Doctors" (20 listed as of October 2026);` llms.txt` says "Licensed US providers" Physicians only (MD, DO or MBBS), never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant


**What you pay** $20 visit fee (60-day window; $10 change or 60-day extension) plus Spot Cream at $36/mo on auto-refill ($452/yr with visit) or $103 once, as of October 2026 $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's price, typically $20 to $100; optional memberships typically $25 to $100/mo


**Subscription required?** 2-month auto-refill or buy-once ($86 to $177 as of October 2026) No subscription required; optional membership for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time


**Where the medicine comes from** Compounded by partner pharmacies and shipped to you (transfers available) The pharmacy you choose, including local and mail-order pharmacies


**Insurance** Not accepted (HSA/FSA accepted) Cash-pay visits; insurance or discount coupon at the pharmacy (with prior authorization help)


**What else the doctor can help with** Skin, hair loss, menopause hormones, longevity; unrelated general problems not stated Other problems in their specialty with the same doctor; every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record


**How you reach them** Musely site or app; no MCP, ChatGPT, or Claude app found futureclinic.com, or from your AI app such as ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, or Grok ([futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) )


**What you get back** Doctor review within 24 hours; in-app "AI powered eNurse Bot" Plan with a Human Signature, plus prescriptions or labs if your doctor decides they fit; replies typically within a few hours, almost always the same day or the next


## Do you want a compounded product menu or a doctor one to one?


Musely (Trusper Inc. DBA Musely) sells its own[compounded prescription products](https://support.musely.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053220473-Can-I-pick-up-my-Musely-prescription-order-from-my-local-pharmacy-or-have-it-transferred-to-an-online-pharmacy) , mixed and shipped by partner pharmacies (transfers available). Per[Musely's llms.txt](https://www.musely.com/llms.txt) as of October 2026, it covers dark spots, melasma, acne, anti-aging, rosacea, hair loss, menopause hormones, and longevity, including oral tranexamic acid, doxycycline, hormone pills, and a "Metformin & CoQ10 Powered Pill for Longevity." Its[doctors page](https://www.musely.com/doctors) lists 20 "Board-Certified Doctors" as of October 2026.


FutureClinic has over 300 doctors across the US. Care spans more than 60 specialties, including dermatologists, family and internal medicine doctors, and other specialists. A dermatologist treating your melasma can also treat rosacea, eczema, or acne in the same chat, and those who offer oral isotretinoin (Accutane) manage it by message, iPLEDGE included. Every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record. (FutureClinic doctors do not prescribe controlled medicines such as stimulants, benzodiazepines, opioids, testosterone, or phentermine.)


## How do the costs compare over a full year?


At Musely, as of October 2026, a[nonrefundable $20 Doctor Visit Fee](https://support.musely.com/hc/en-us/articles/360048332334-What-is-the-20-Doctor-Visit-Fee-for) covers 60 days of messaging, with a[$10 fee](https://support.musely.com/hc/en-us/articles/5676361491479-Breakdown-of-Doctor-Visit-Fees-What-is-the-fee-for) for a prescription change or 60-day extension. Creams ship free on a 2-month[auto-refill plan](https://support.musely.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500007186021-How-can-I-cancel-Auto-Refill) or once: as of October 2026,[The Spot Cream](https://www.musely.com/spotcream) is $36/mo ($103 once),[The Acne Cream](https://www.musely.com/acnecream) is $30/mo ($86 once), and[The Red Set](https://www.musely.com/redset) is $62/mo ($177 once). Musely[does not accept insurance](https://support.musely.com/hc/en-us/articles/13757532403223-Do-you-accept-insurance) , so a year of The Spot Cream on auto-refill plus the $20 visit fee costs $452.


At FutureClinic, there is no[subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) required. A visit is $40 for the best-fit doctor, or you can choose a specific doctor at their listed fee, typically $20 to $100. For a stable medicine, when your doctor judges it safe, they can prescribe several months at once to the pharmacy you choose, where insurance (with prior authorization help) or a texted discount coupon applies. For ongoing care, most physicians offer an optional membership (typically $25 to $100/mo, $50 median) with unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time, and your initial visit fee counts toward it if you join afterward.
